title: The Old man at the gate
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：old　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 old 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the observer wrote of ① an old man at the gate in the log, and everybody in the observatory said at once that it was ② older than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the observer, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the old ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the oldest man at the gate anybody in the observatory had ever seen, or so the log for November 1983 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too old to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the assistant who had come to help; the old ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the lens at the far dome, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an old coat on the hook, and said that no assistant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as old as the coat on the hook they had once had in the old observatory. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was old or not, and he said so.

By 1996 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the log. What the line asked for was ⑦ something old, and nothing besides. The assistant from the next observatory called the whole plan ⑧ quite old; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the log kept the names of the old ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1999, in the rain, she wrote of another old man at the gate in the same log, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ older than anybody had expected. ⑩ The oldest coat on the hook in the whole observatory, she said in 2001, was the one she could never quite name; the old ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 年老（前置定语 an old man at the gate：1989 年观测员在观测记录里记下的那件年老的老人）
B. adj. 年老／旧（比较级 older than：文中两处，一处比门口的老人，一处比预想）
C. adj. 年老／旧（最高级 the oldest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 年老（表语 too old to do：母亲觉得它太年老，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 旧（前置定语 an old coat on the hook：叔叔把整件事称作一桩旧的钩子上那件旧外套）
F. adj. 旧（同级比较 as old as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩钩子上那件旧外套相比）
G. adj. 旧（后置定语 something old：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 旧（受程度副词修饰 quite old：那位助手的评价）

items.q: an old man at the gate
the oldest man at the gate anybody
an old coat on the hook
The oldest coat on the hook in

answers.why: old 意为“年老”，1989 年观测员在观测记录里记下的是“一件年老的老人”，此处作前置定语 an old man at the gate。
old 意为“年老”，此处用比较级 older than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
old 意为“年老”，观测记录上 十一月 那行字说它是观测站里最年老的一件，故用最高级 the oldest man at the gate。
old 意为“年老”，母亲认为这件东西“太年老了，谁也用不上”，too old to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
old 意为“旧”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩旧的钩子上那件旧外套”，此处作前置定语 an old coat on the hook。
old 意为“旧”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩钩子上那件旧外套一样旧”，同级比较用 as old as。
old 意为“旧”，观测记录上那半行字要的是“旧的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something old。
old 意为“旧”，邻观测站来的那位助手认为这套计划“相当旧”，quite 修饰原级 old。
old 意为“旧”，1999 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要旧”，故用比较级 older than。
old 意为“旧”，母亲 2001 年说的是“整个观测站里最旧的那一桩”，故用最高级 the oldest coat on the hook。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1989 年，观测员在观测记录里记下了一件年老的老人。（an old man at the gate）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更年老。（older than …）
母亲觉得它太年老，谁也用不上。（too old to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩旧的钩子上那件旧外套。（an old coat on the hook）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩钩子上那件旧外套一样旧。（as old as …）
到了 1996 年，观测记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件旧的东西。（something old）
answers: In 1989 the observer wrote of an old man at the gate in the log.
Everybody said it was older than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too old to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an old coat on the hook.
He said nobody would call it as old as the coat on the hook they had once had.
By 1996 the log asked for nothing but something old.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 old 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1989 the observer wrote of an old man at the gate in the log, and nobody forgot it.
It was the oldest man at the gate in the observatory, or so the log says.
My mother thought it too old to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an old coat on the hook, and nobody argued with him.
The assistant from the next observatory called the plan quite old, and everybody laughed.
The old ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
